questions.question: Which one is NOT protective riding gear?
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a leather or sturdy jacket, leather or sturdy pants, boots that cover your ankles, and hearing protection.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for your friend.
Keep your friend busy with other activities.
Stop your friend from leaving until they are sober.
Let your friend ride their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let your friend ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Never let an impaired friend ride. You can arrange another ride, keep them busy, prevent them from leaving early, or ask other friends to help stop them from riding.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before starting your motorcycle. Position them so you can see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane beside you.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes, not the rest of your face. A windshield is not a replacement for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch located?
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is next to the right handgrip. Learn where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: What happens if your front tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: The steering will feel the same.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If your steering suddenly feels heavy, pull off the road and check your tires.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection by itself.

questions.question: What happens when your rear tire skids?

options.text: You lose the ability to change direction.
It is only dangerous if the front tire also skids.

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose the ability to change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a serious crash. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel and removes your ability to steer. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: How do you maintain control while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.

questions.explanation: Look through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before turning and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: What should you do to prevent an accident?

options.text: Follow the vehicle ahead very closely.
Focus only on your controls and not ahead.
Signal your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Be visible to others by using your signals, brake light, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and jam the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the front brake lever and press the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when slowing down or stopping.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:

options.text: You can see through the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.explanation: Leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see ahead clearly, or if traffic is heavy. More space gives you time to stop safely.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Know where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in a group. When the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with palm facing back, the group should stop.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, you should use both brakes:

options.text: Only if the pavement is wet.
Only when riding in the city.

questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the best stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always avoid the left portion of a lane.
Always avoid the right portion of a lane.
Always avoid the center portion of a lane.
Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position to always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Move to the leftmost portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Stay calm and ride straight at a steady speed. Weaving to match the motion will make it worse.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, you may need to:

options.text: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting safely.
Flash your brakes to alert drivers behind you about downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down before shifting to a lower gear. Downshifting while going too fast can cause the motorcycle to lurch and the rear wheel to skid. Use brakes to reach a safe speed before downshifting on hills or when shifting into first gear.

questions.question: When a group of riders is passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, the riders should:

options.text: Pass in a staggered formation with several riders passing at the same time.

questions.explanation: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, riders should pass one at a time. Each rider must complete their pass before the next rider begins.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop sign then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop sign, then move forward to see cross traffic better.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then move forward to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop line first. Then edge forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Riders can use hand signals instead of mechanical turn signals. When a rider extends their left arm straight out, it means they plan to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: Switching to a lower gear is also called:
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear works like braking. This is why downshifting is also called engine braking.

questions.question: Studies show that when motorcycles have their headlights on during the day:

options.text: They are harder to see than other vehicles.
Other drivers see them better than when headlights are off.
They are less safe than when headlights are off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers see them better than when headlights are off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride to help other drivers see you. A motorcycle with its headlight on during the day is twice as likely to be noticed.

questions.question: The front brake should be:

options.text: Used sometimes to help the rear brake.
Used together with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Used together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both the front and rear brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: To avoid serious injury, you should wear all of the following except:
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high and sturdy boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves.
